label: es-e4b5
change: The UIKit host (iPad and Apple TV) becomes the engine library NTSDUIKitHost (with NTSD_IOS=1; NTSDCore, NTSDRuntime; UIKit, AVFoundation, CoreText): NTSDApp.swift (app and scene delegates, view controller, game view) and NTSDiOSHost.swift (window host, music player, session host) by git mv, the session host taking the OriginalGame instead of NTSDContent, and the former NTSDiOS main (the --events-file redirect, UIApplicationMain with the app delegate) as NTSDUIKitHost.run(game:), which keeps the game in a module global for the scene delegate UIKit creates. The game's NTSDiOS is one call. The packagers' Info.plist names the scene delegate by its new module (NTSDUIKitHost.NTSDSceneDelegate; ios_app.py, ios_device.py).

review.verdict: no required fix: the entry keeps the redirect and UIApplicationMain; the scene configuration's explicit delegateClass wins for a new session, the plist change keeps the manifest naming a real class; launchedGame is set before UIApplicationMain and so before any scene connects; the moved files reach the game only through the OriginalGame; manifests and tvOS branches unchanged in effect
review.question: a scene session saved by an earlier build could carry the old delegate class on an install over it
review.answer: the iPad app's saved session (Library/Saved Application State/local.ntsd.native.ios.savedState/KnownSceneSessions, written 2026-10-18 by an earlier build) archives only the configuration name 'Default', the role and the session identifier, no class: a restored session resolves its delegate through the Info.plist by that name, so the plist change is the one that keeps such installs working; the iPad rows installed over that app (simctl install keeps the data container) and passed
adopted: the live TVOS_WEB description of the Apple TV host names NTSDUIKitHost (the dated 'Verified starting point' section is history and stays)
notAdopted: @MainActor on run(game:): only matters under strict concurrency (as for the AppKit host)
